title: How AI writes
blurb: Train your own tiny ChatGPT. Feed it text, watch it learn to guess the next word, then make it write.

steps.title: The magic trick behind ChatGPT
steps.body:
Chatbots can write stories, answer questions, even rhyme. It feels like magic.

But the secret is almost silly: a chatbot is just **guessing the next word**, over and over. Say a few words, and it asks itself *"what word usually comes next?"* — picks one — then does it again. That's it. You're about to build the smallest possible version and see for yourself.

steps.title: Words become tokens
steps.body:
Before an AI can work with language, it chops the text into little pieces called **tokens**. For us, a token is just a **word** (and punctuation like `.` or `?`).

"the cat sat" → `the` · `cat` · `sat`. Simple. Now the AI can count which tokens tend to follow which.

steps.title: Predict the next word
steps.body:
Here's the whole idea. The model reads a lot of text and keeps a tally:

After **"the cat"**, what came next? Maybe `sat` 5 times, `ran` 2 times, `is` 1 time.

So when you give it "the cat", it knows `sat` is the most likely next word. **Training** is just building that tally — no magic, just counting.

steps.title: How far back does it look?
steps.body:
The **context window** is how many previous words the model looks at to make its guess.

Look back **1 word** and it barely makes sense. Look back **3 words** and it sounds much smoother — but on a little bit of text it starts to just **memorize and repeat**. Real LLMs look back over *thousands* of tokens. You'll get to slide this and feel the difference.

steps.title: Train it and make it write
steps.body:
1) Pick some text and press **Train it**. 2) Peek at the **next-word table** — that's literally what it learned. 3) Type a start and press **Generate**.

Then play: change **Look back** (1 → 3 words) and re-train. Watch the writing get smoother but more repetitive.

steps.title: What is it really doing?
steps.question: When a language model writes a sentence, what is it actually doing at each step?
choices: Looking up the answer in a dictionary
Guessing the next word, then repeating
Asking a human what to say
steps.explain: Every word is a next-word guess based on the words so far. Do that again and again and you get whole sentences.

steps.title: Creativity = temperature
steps.body:
When several words could come next, how does it choose? That's the **creativity** knob (pros call it *temperature*).

**Careful**: it almost always picks the single most likely word — safe but repetitive. **Wild**: it takes more chances on less-likely words — surprising, sometimes nonsense. Slide it and watch the next-word table change shape.

steps.title: Play with creativity
steps.body: Train it, then move the **Creativity** slider and Generate a few times. Low = it repeats the safe path. High = it wanders. Notice the next-word percentages flatten out as you turn creativity up.

steps.title: Turning up creativity
steps.question: If you turn the creativity (temperature) way up, what happens?
choices: It always picks the most likely word
It takes more chances on less-likely words, so output is more surprising
It looks back at more words
steps.explain: High creativity flattens the odds so unlikely words get picked more often — fun, but it can drift into nonsense.

steps.title: So what is 'training'?
steps.question: You trained your model. What did training actually build?
choices: A tally of which words tend to follow which
steps.explain: Training = counting patterns (which word follows which). Real LLMs store this as billions of weights, but it's the same idea you just did.

steps.title: Same idea, gigantic scale
steps.body:
You just built a real language model: tokens, next-word prediction, a context window, and a creativity knob.

ChatGPT is the **exact same recipe** — scaled up almost unimaginably. Instead of a few rhymes it read much of the internet; instead of a tally it uses a giant neural network with billions of weights (the same weights you tuned in *How a brain learns*). But peek inside and it's doing what your tiny model just did: **guess the next word, then repeat**. You now understand how AI writes. 🎉
